key_insight: Tuning Ti-substituted SrVO₃ toward a metal–insulator transition broadens its optical window, with the best transparency–conductivity balance found near the transition.
engineering_relevance: This materials-design strategy could improve transparent electrodes for silicon photovoltaics by balancing optical transmission against electrical transport.
method: Tune Ti substitution in epitaxial SrVO₃ films.
Evaluate optical transparency, metallic transport, and near-Fermi-level spectral weight.
Use the Haacke figure of merit to identify the optimal composition range.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic optical-window broadening and a figure-of-merit optimum near the transition, where metallic transport is lost despite persistent near-Fermi-level spectral weight.
watch_item: Carrier depletion and disorder undermine coherent transport near the transition; the abstract does not report solar-cell device performance or AI-based methods.
paper_title: Engineering Correlated Transparent Conductors via Metal-Insulator Transition Proximity
